title: Streaming + Tool Interop Playbook for Developer SDKs (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for how the Hosted API should expose progressive streaming, tool interop, and structured output to developer-facing SDKs. The goal is to create a small set of ergonomic primitives that make it easy for application engineers to: (1) receive partial results quickly, (2) interleave tool calls deterministically, and (3) consume typed/structured payloads without brittle parsing.

This doc focuses on the SDK-facing contract (REST/WS + SDK surfaces) rather than low-level runtime implementation. It is explicitly a developer ergonomics PRD: protocols and examples that SDK teams can implement and maintain across languages.

Primary goals:
- Reliable progressive output semantics: deliver tokens/partial payloads with clear finalization markers and stable ordering.
- Lightweight tool call choreography: allow model to request external actions and for the client to satisfy them with minimal plumbing.
- Structured payloads without blocking: support JSON-like typed chunks that can be validated/consumed incrementally.
- Predictable backpressure and reconnect semantics for long-lived streams.
- Low-friction SDK APIs that map naturally to idiomatic patterns in JS/Python/Go.

Non-goals (for now):
- Defining a canonical schema language for all structured outputs (we’ll support JSON-first + optional schema hints).
- Replacing customer-specific orchestration frameworks. We will provide primitives to integrate with those.

User personas and journeys:
- Product engineer (frontend) wiring streaming to show progressive UI. Wants incremental deltas, clear final event, and lightweight cancellation.
- Backend workflow engineer using tool calls to orchestrate external lookups (calendar, DB) triggered by the model with reliable retry semantics.
- Platform integrator embedding Redwood in serverless flows needing deterministic structured outputs for downstream rules.

Key design principles:
- Explicit events, not opaque tokens: streams must emit typed events (token, structured_chunk, tool_request, tool_result, done, error) so SDKs can switch behavior based on event type.
- Idempotency and correlation: tool requests include stable ids and optional replay tokens so clients and Redwood runtime can deduplicate.
- Small surface, language-idiomatic: expose a minimal core in each SDK (e.g., async iterator in JS/Python, channel in Go) and provide helpers for higher-level patterns.
- Backwards-friendly: streaming must gracefully degrade to non-streaming responses for older clients.

Protocol sketch (high level)
- Transport: support both HTTP/1.1 chunked (for sync fallback) and WebSocket/HTTP2 for higher-perf streaming.
- Event framing: newline-delimited JSON events (ndjson) for simplicity and easy parsing in most runtimes. Each event is a top-level object with keys: id, type, payload, ts, final (bool).

Sample event types and minimal fields (developer-facing contract)
- token: incremental text fragment from model. payload.text
- structured_chunk: partial structured result. payload.data (stringified JSON fragment) payload.path_hint (optional)
- tool_request: model asks client to run external action. payload.tool (string) payload.input (JSON) request_id (string)
- tool_result: client returns result for a tool_request. payload.result (JSON) request_id (string)
- control.done: final marker for response. payload.summary (optional)
- control.error: structured error with code/retryable/message

Example ndjson stream (illustrative)
{"id":"r1","type":"token","payload":{"text":"Finding flights…"},"ts":"2025-03-04T12:01:02Z","final":false}
{"id":"r1","type":"tool_request","payload":{"tool":"flight_search","input":{"from":"SFO","to":"JFK","date":"2025-04-02"},"request_id":"req-42"},"ts":"2025-03-04T12:01:02Z","final":false}
// client runs search, posts tool_result
{"id":"r1","type":"tool_result","payload":{"result":{"offers":[{"id":"A1","price":199}]},"request_id":"req-42"},"ts":"2025-03-04T12:01:03Z","final":false}
{"id":"r1","type":"structured_chunk","payload":{"data":"{\"itinerary\":{\"legs\":[]}}","path_hint":"response.itinerary"},"ts":"2025-03-04T12:01:04Z","final":false}
{"id":"r1","type":"control.done","payload":{},"ts":"2025-03-04T12:01:05Z","final":true}

SDK ergonomics (JS/Python/Go notes)
- JS (node/browser): primary API is an async iterator that yields event objects. Helpers: toTextStream(iterable) concatenates token events; toStructured(iterable) accumulates structured_chunk pieces and validates JSON at path_hints. Provide convenience wrappers to auto-ack tool_request and call a registered tool handler.

Pseudo-API (JS)
const stream = await client.stream({model: 'rw-x', input})
for await (const ev of stream) {
  if (ev.type === 'token') render(ev.payload.text)
  if (ev.type === 'tool_request') {
    const res = await handlers[ev.payload.tool](ev.payload.input)
    await stream.sendToolResult(ev.payload.request_id, res)
  }
  if (ev.type === 'control.done') break
}

- Python: async iterator + sync iterator variants. Provide built-in backpressure-aware send_tool_result(request_id, result). Also provide a sync convenience: client.stream_to_file(...).

- Go: channel-based API returning events with typed enums. Helper library for common tool patterns (blocking vs fire-and-forget).

Tool-calling semantics and guarantees
- At-most-once vs at-least-once: default is at-most-once for tool execution to avoid side-effect duplication. Offer an explicit header flag tool_execution: at_least_once to allow retries when caller can handle idempotency.
- Correlation: request_id is required and stable. Server may re-emit a prior tool_request after reconnects unless client acknowledges (ack id via sendToolResult).
- Timeout and fallback: clients may return a special tool_result with {"error":"TIMEOUT"} to signal failure; the model can then choose an alternate action.

Structured output patterns
- Progressive JSON assembly: structured_chunk fragments are appended and should be valid when concatenated, but we will not require fragments to be self-contained JSON objects. SDK to provide incremental parser with path_hint assistance.
- Path hints: small strings indicating target JSON path (dot-separated) so SDKs can stream chunks into the right path and validate incrementally.
- Small typed envelope: every final response should include an envelope: {"status":"ok","payload":...,"meta":{}} for predictable downstream parsing.

Backpressure, reconnects, and fault modes
- Client-driven window: servers emit up to N concurrent events; clients can send flow control messages (window_increment) to increase capacity. Default N=16 events pending. Implementations should tune based on latency.
- Reconnects: server should persist recent stream state for short windows (30s) to allow seamless reconnects; if not possible, SDKs should fall back to non-streaming retry.
- Partial persistence: tool_request/response correlation prevents duplicate side-effects; clients can recover by re-sending a sendToolResult with request_id and the same payload and set replay_token when appropriate.

Telemetry and observability
- Emit structured telemetry events for: time-to-first-token, time-to-final, number of tool calls, average tool latency, structured_chunk count, reconnect events, decode errors.
- SDKs should surface these metrics and attach them to Redwood tracing headers to correlate with server-side traces.

Migration and rollout plan
- Phase 0 (canary): implement ndjson framing + token events in JS SDK, enable opt-in header in Hosted API. Test with internal apps (chat playground, support bot).
- Phase 1 (broader): add tool_request/tool_result patterns and structured_chunk. Enable in 25% of traffic for customers who opt in.
- Phase 2 (GA): all SDKs support event types, provide official migration guides and back-compat helpers (non-streaming fallbacks, polyfills).

Compatibility notes
- Older SDKs receive a plain non-streaming JSON blob if they do not set the streaming flag; we will document feature detection.
- Provide a reference polyfill that turns server-sent events into the async-iterator contract for older browsers/environments.

Open questions (bikeshedding candidates)
- Exact ndjson event schema: should we add a "version" field and an extensible metadata sub-object? (Recommended: yes, start with v1).
- Tool execution default semantics: is at-most-once acceptable for most customers? We need SRE/product input.
- Chunk validity model: should fragments be guaranteed to be JSON-suffix-safe (so that concatenation always yields valid JSON)? That makes runtime more complex.
- Should SDK auto-retry tool_result submission on transient network errors or surface that to the app?

Next steps and owners
- Product: ship this playbook as the canonical SDK contract (owner: Maya Chen).
- SDK leads: implement JS polyfill and iterator API for internal use (owner: Priya Nair).
- Applied ML / runtime: add server-side ndjson event emitter and short-term stream state (owner: Diego Alvarez).
- SRE: review at-most-once semantics and suggest defaults for safety (owner: Sofia Petrov).

Appendix: quick sample (JS helper pseudo)
async function handleStream(resp) {
  for await (const ev of resp.stream()) {
    switch(ev.type) {
      case 'token': process.stdout.write(ev.payload.text); break;
      case 'tool_request':
        const out = await callTool(ev.payload.tool, ev.payload.input);
        await resp.sendToolResult(ev.payload.request_id, out);
        break;
      case 'structured_chunk': mergeStructured(ev.payload); break;
      case 'control.done': return;
    }
  }
}

References and related work:
- internal: confluence:hosted-api-streaming-playbook-v1
- RFCs: INF-1423 (streaming baseline), INF-1470 (tool call runtimes)

Status: draft — still iterating on event schema and tool semantics. Feedback requested from SDK leads, applied-ml, and SRE.
